items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: What exactly is this ₹107-crore thing I keep hearing about?
items.answer: RTFF & SDSS — a sensor network + weather models + maps fused into a dashboard that promises street-level flood forecasts 72 hours ahead. REPORT §1–2.

items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: Who runs it day to day?
items.answer: The Hydro-Modelling Control Room at the State EOC (Ezhilagam) under the Commissionerate of Revenue Administration / TNDRRA; consultant SECON–JBA runs modelling during activations; Flood Monitoring Centres sit in district collectorates. CFM AboutUs.

items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: Where is it physically?
items.answer: HMCR at SEOC Ezhilagam; FMCs at GCC, Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Ranipet collectorates; a disaster-recovery centre proposed at WRD Chepauk. CFM AboutUs.

items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: When did it start?
items.answer: Conceived after the 2015 flood; piloted NEM 2021; "operationalized" NEM 2022 and 2023 (Current Science, Jul 2024); declared "fully operational" Oct 2025.

items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: Is it really India's first?
items.answer: Billed "first fully operational comprehensive urban FF-DSS" in launch coverage (graded B/C in our ledger). Mumbai's CFLOWS predates it in research; "first" depends on definitions nobody has fixed.

items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: Does it predict floods or just record them?
items.answer: Design says predict (72-hour street-level). Evidence says it *records* well (F8) and predicting is publicly unverifiable (F5). Both halves verified in our mirror.

items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: Which areas does it cover?
items.answer: 4,974 km² across Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Ranipet — the Adyar, Cooum, Kosasthalaiyar and Kovalam basins.

items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: Is my district inside?
items.answer: If you're in those five districts, yes on paper. Exact per-ward sensor coverage: check the station registries in our `chennai-flood-monitor-transactions` dataset.

items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: Who built it?
items.answer: SECON Private Ltd (Bangalore) + JBA Consulting (UK) as a JV; IIT Madras provided technical supervision; TNUIFSL managed the money.

items.section: A. The system in plain terms
items.q: Chennai flooded in 2005, 2015, 2021, 2023 — why did the brain only arrive in 2025?
items.answer: The 2015 flood created the political mandate and the World Bank money pipe; the build took ~5 years; press calls it "operational" only from Oct 2025. History: ELI10 §2A. ---

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: How much did it cost, finally?
items.answer: ₹107.2 crore — press figure at launch (ledger row 10, graded C).

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: Was that always the price?
items.answer: No. Nov 2022 press reported **₹71 crore**; Oct 2025 launch reported ₹107.2 crore — **+51% in three years**, no public revision order (ledger row 22).

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: Where can I read the sanction order?
items.answer: Not published anywhere we can find. **RTI target #1:** WRD / CRA / Finance Dept for the G.O. sanctioning RTFF & SDSS under PDGF.

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: Is it grant money or loan money?
items.answer: Both, layered: World Bank *loan* to GoI→GoTN, repackaged as PDGF *grant* for consultancies (REPORT §5).

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: Who repays the World Bank?
items.answer: GoTN, via GoI, in hard currency — FX risk on the state budget, 20–32-year maturities observed in the TN portfolio.

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: How does ₹107.2 cr split between software, sensors, surveys, IIT-M?
items.answer: No public split. **RTI target:** SECON–JBA contract schedules + PDGF utilisation certificates.

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: What is PDGF in one line?
items.answer: The government's own "grant shop" at TNUIFSL — a non-lapsable technical-assistance fund fed by World Bank/KfW/JICA/ADB project lines, operational 1 Apr 2015.

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: How big is PDGF next to this one project?
items.answer: PDGF disbursed ₹52.64 cr in 2023-24 — *across all assignments*. RTFF & SDSS cost ~2 years of the entire fund's output.

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: Is the World Bank still paying for it?
items.answer: Yes — TNCRUDP (P179189) procurement plans (Dec 2023, Dec 2024) list RTFF "handholding supervision" ($0.10M) and satellite DEM/DSM work ($0.36M).

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: Was there competitive bidding for the consultant?
items.answer: TNUIFSL uses QCBS/direct-selection routes; the actual RTFF award method and bids are not public. **RTI target:** TNUIFSL tender file.

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: What's the annual operations budget?
items.answer: Never published. No O&M line exists publicly — a headline gap (F10).

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: What does it cost per km², per ward?
items.answer: ₹2.16 lakh/km²; ₹53.6 lakh per ward. Whether that's good value depends on verification — which doesn't exist (F5).

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: Is the money spent, or still flowing?
items.answer: Build-phase money spent (₹107.2 cr claim); aftercare money still flowing via TNCRUDP IPF-TA assignments.

items.section: B. Money: sanction, cost and the creep
items.q: Who can audit this spend?
items.answer: CAG can, on its own initiative or on demand; no CAG report on this line is public. **Ask:** include RTFF & SDSS in a performance audit. ---

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: Does the World Bank lend to Chennai directly?
items.answer: No — IBRD lends only to sovereign governments. Chennai's system is financed through GoI→GoTN chains.

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: What interest rate did Tamil Nadu pay?
items.answer: IBRD pricing is benchmark-plus-spread with fees; the specific rate for the PDGF-feeding projects isn't published at this layer. Loan agreements (public at WB) carry it.

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: How long does repayment take?
items.answer: Observed TN instruments: 32-yr maturity/7-yr grace (TNCRUDP 2023), 23-yr/6.5-yr (SHORE 2025), 20-yr/3.5-yr (housing DPLs). Your flood brain sits on decades of sovereign debt.

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: What is "Program-for-Results"?
items.answer: A WB instrument that disburses only against independently verified program results — verification is a payment condition.

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: Does the current program verify forecast accuracy as a result?
items.answer: Nothing public shows RTFF performance indicators in the TNCRUDP results framework. **RTI/watch:** the PforR DLR schedule and ISRs.

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: Can citizens read the loan agreement?
items.answer: World Bank loan agreements and DLR schedules are published on its website — a no-RTI ask once signed.

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: Has the Bank funded TN flood/urban work before?
items.answer: Yes — TNUDP I–III (1990s–2006, incl. $300M TNUDP III), TN & Puducherry Coastal DRR ($236M, 2013), TNSUDP ($400M IBRD, 2015), now TNCRUDP ($300M, 2023).

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: What is the Inspection Panel?
items.answer: The World Bank's independent accountability mechanism — affected people can request investigation of WB-financed projects.

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: What else has PDGF bought over the years?
items.answer: Annual utilisation statements exist at TNUIFSL (₹35–122 cr/yr inflows); itemised assignment lists are patchy. **RTI target:** PDGF statements naming RTFF & SDSS.

items.section: C. The World Bank and the terms of lending
items.q: Is the "grant" framing misleading?
items.answer: At the project level, no one repays — but one layer up it is sovereign debt. The costume matters for disclosure: grants skip the investment-project disclosure stack (REPORT §5.4.3). ---

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: Who is SECON?
items.answer: A Bangalore survey/water-resources engineering firm; project consultant (planning, setup, commissioning) and web-DSS developer.

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: Who is JBA?
items.answer: JBA Consulting (UK) — a flood-risk consultancy whose parent sells flood models to the re/insurance industry.

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: What did the SECON–JBA contract cost?
items.answer: Not public. **RTI target #2:** the JV's contract value and payment schedule.

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: Are there other vendors?
items.answer: Yes — station registries we mirrored carry AMC (maintenance) vendor-name fields; the hardware sensor vendors are also in the registry stack.

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: What is IIT-M's contract?
items.answer: "Technical supervision" per official text; the value and terms of IIT-M's engagement are not public.

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: When do the maintenance contracts expire?
items.answer: 66 stations carry `isamc=true` flags, but expiry dates are populated for only ~6 — the O&M calendar is unknown even to its own registry (F10).

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: What happens when an AMC lapses?
items.answer: No published plan. **Watch:** our AMC-expiry calendar (AUDIT-PLAN B2).

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: Were the tenders published?
items.answer: TN e-procurement notices and WB procurement plans exist in fragments; no consolidated public list of RTFF contracts.

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: Were conflict-of-interest checks done?
items.answer: Nothing public.

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: Who owns the system's software IP?
items.answer: RTI target: contract IP clauses.

items.section: D. Contracts, consultants and vendors
items.q: Is the same JV involved in the new IFMC?
items.answer: Not stated in Oct 2026 coverage. **Watch:** IFMC procurement trail. ---

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: How many sensors are there?
items.answer: Registries we mirror: 328 ARG (incl. IIT-M 61 + 87 proposed), 121 AWLR existing + 139 basin-proposed, 63+53 SRG (GCC+PWD), 39+13 AWS, 5 gate sensors, plus tidal, agro, groundwater stations.

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Are they all working?
items.answer: On census day: 22 of 38 dashboard stations fresh — 16 stale (F2).

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: What about Nungambakkam, THE Chennai rain gauge?
items.answer: Frozen at **10 May 2025** — 16+ months of nothing on the system built to show exactly that (F2).

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Who checks the sensors' health?
items.answer: No public QA process; our mirror shows impossible values that nobody flagged (F7).

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: What's a gate sensor for?
items.answer: It reads lake/shutter positions — input to reservoir-release decisions (LoGS).

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: What's an AWLR?
items.answer: Automatic Water Level Recorder — telemetry on rivers, canals, tanks.

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Are sensor locations public?
items.answer: Yes — coordinates are in the registry layers (our mirror publishes them as maps).

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Are there sensors near me?
items.answer: Likely, if you're in the 5 districts — verify against the ARG/AWLR registry maps in our GIS release.

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Why did a sensor read −18 °C in Chennai?
items.answer: Data-quality failure at Kattupakkam (F7) — and nobody at the system flagged it. That's the point of F7.

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Who physically fixes a dead gauge?
items.answer: Per-station maintenance responsibility is not published (AMC fields sparse).

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Is there a public sensor-status page?
items.answer: No — recommendation #3 asks for exactly that.

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: How old is this network?
items.answer: Rain records reach back to 1976 (SRG archive); the modern telemetry network is largely a 2018–2021 install.

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Did the 639 mm in one day at Michaung really happen?
items.answer: Yes — it's in our rescued predecessor archive: 639 mm/24 h at the Zone-12 (Meenambakkam 6A) gauge, 2023-12-04 (ledger row 12, grade A).

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Can I watch live sensor data right now?
items.answer: The dashboard shows day-cards only; the machine-readable open feed is stale (F3). Our mirror is point-in-time.

items.section: E. The sensor network
items.q: Do all districts have equal sensor density?
items.answer: No published density analysis. Compute it yourself from our registries — that's what they're for. ---

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Is the system's data "open data"?
items.answer: Accidentally, yes (F1) — 343 of 344 GeoServer layers answer anonymous queries; but with no license, no docs, no promise it stays.

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Can I download bulk data from the government?
items.answer: No bulk facility exists. Bulk is available from **our** Hugging Face mirrors.

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: What license governs the government's data?
items.answer: None published. Our release carries CC BY 4.0 on our arrangements; we claim no rights over the facts.

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Is there an API?
items.answer: An undocumented GeoServer + ~60 AJAX endpoints exist; the only "API reference" is our census (REPORT §3).

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Did you hack the system?
items.answer: No. Read-only requests, identical to what the public website's own browser session issues. No logins, no bypassing.

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Is what you did legal?
items.answer: Raw telemetry isn't copyrightable; NDSAP 2012 makes this class of data open by default; §52 fair dealing covers research/reporting (REPORT §6, ELI10 §9).

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Where do I get your data?
items.answer: Hugging Face: `CashlessConsumer/chennai-flood-monitor-transactions`, `chennaidss-gis-layers`, `chennai-flood-history`, `chennai-flood-bulletins`, `chennai-rain-gauges`.

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: What formats?
items.answer: Parquet/GeoParquet — one-line DuckDB queries; GeoJSON source dumps also on disk.

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Is personal data in your release?
items.answer: Scrubbed: officer names, SIM/mobile columns, citizen usernames removed (DATA-CATALOGUE §1, gis-layers README).

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Could the government switch the leak off?
items.answer: Yes — and that's F1's warning. Our annual re-mirror and the public release are the hedge.

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Why does open data matter for a flood?
items.answer: Because independent verification, third-party apps, journalism, and research all need it. A warning you can't independently check is a rumour with a logo.

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: What's a GeoServer?
items.answer: Standard open-source map-data server software; the pretty website is a skin over it.

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: What are the 344 layers, in groups?
items.answer: DATA-CATALOGUE §3: transactions (13), station registries (31), water (34), drainage (8), boundaries (24), wards/crowd/alerts (8), flood history (9), forecast surfaces (37), misc bulletin wrappers (35).

items.section: F. Open data and public access
items.q: Has anything changed since you mirrored?
items.answer: Re-census 2026-10-03: still exactly 344 layers, zero added/removed (DATA-CATALOGUE §1). ---

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: Does it really give 3-day street-level warnings?
items.answer: The design says so and the Oct-2025 bulletins (image PDFs) show street-flood maps for the activation window. Publicly verifiable, continuously? No (F4/F5).

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: How far ahead does it look?
items.answer: 72 hours — five weather models fused with real-time sensor data.

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: Which weather models does it fuse?
items.answer: ECMWF, NCEP-GFS, UKMet, IMD-GFS and NCMRWF ensembles (AboutUs).

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: What's an "ensemble"?
items.answer: The same model run many ways (P25…P95 percentiles) — a range, not a single number.

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: Are the forecasts saved anywhere?
items.answer: **No archive exists.** The single most damning gap (F5). Forecast side must be captured activation-by-activation going forward.

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: So how accurate is it?
items.answer: No public forecast-vs-observed record exists — the ₹107-crore question with no public answer (F5).

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: Which areas get street-level forecasts?
items.answer: Named vulnerable zones: Pulianthope, Nungambakkam, Mambalam, Saidapet, Velachery, Meenambakkam, Mudichur.

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: What about my ward specifically?
items.answer: The only public ward-depth layer is **static, stamped 11 Aug 2021** (F4) — a five-monsoon-old scenario, not a live forecast.

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: What is LoGS?
items.answer: Lake & Reservoir Operation Guidance System — advises WRD on shutter releases to reduce peaks while saving drinking water.

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: Does it model storm-water drains?
items.answer: The SWD network is a model input (GIS layer in our mirror). But drains must physically work — a model can't desilt.

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: Can I see an actual sample forecast?
items.answer: Yes — all 7 bulletins are on Hugging Face (`chennai-flood-bulletins`), incl. B5.0 Street Flood Inundation (ECMWF P75).

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: Why are bulletins image-only PDFs?
items.answer: Never explained; it makes machine verification impossible. Recommendation: publish data, not pictures.

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: Did the IIT-M research model actually get used?
items.answer: Citizen Matters reports IIT-M's 4-km, 7-ensemble model is integrated and daily forecasts go to GCC/WRD; independent accuracy checks don't exist publicly.

items.section: G. The forecasts themselves
items.q: Is there a floodplain map I can use?
items.answer: 2D model areas, bathymetry, contours are in our GIS mirror — the model's own working surfaces. ---

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: How would I personally get warned?
items.answer: Three routes today: press bulletins during activations, the TN-Alert mobile app, and TNSMART for departments. No SMS/RSS/API spec is public.

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: Is there an SMS blast?
items.answer: No public spec or evidence.

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: Does TN-Alert cost me anything?
items.answer: App is free; the data cost is yours — a small but real equity point.

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: Does the public alert feed work?
items.answer: It has returned **zero rows on every check** (F6).

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: What's "alert equity"?
items.answer: If the only channel is one app you must have installed and open, the poorest, least-connected, most flood-exposed residents are the least served.

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: Will I actually get a warning three days early?
items.answer: Unverifiable — and during Ditwah (Dec 2025) not one media reference credited this system with any warning reaching anyone (MEDIA-CLAIMS pattern 2).

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: Do school closures come from this system?
items.answer: No — collectors act on IMD alerts; RTFF wasn't visibly in that chain in Dec 2025.

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: Do elderly/disabled residents get targeted alerts?
items.answer: No evidence of any differentiated-alert design.

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: Are alerts in Tamil?
items.answer: TN-Alert is claimed multilingual; the bulletins are English-only PDFs.

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: Who decides when to issue an alert?
items.answer: HMCR feeds CRA/departments via TNSMART; the SOP and sign-off chain are not public.

items.section: H. Alerts and warning delivery
items.q: Can I subscribe to alerts myself?
items.answer: No public subscription mechanism exists. ---

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: Did it work in the Dec 2025 Ditwah flood?
items.answer: As a *recorder*: yes — citizen level-6 report at Puzhal, bridge sensors peaking (Aminjikarai 7.705 m, Manali 2.501 m), all consistent with press (F8). As a *forecaster*: unverifiable (F5).

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: And Michaung (Dec 2023)?
items.answer: System was in pilot/operational transition; our predecessor mirror holds the full 639 mm event; no public forecast scorecard exists.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.answer: "Operationalized" per the Current Science paper; no public evaluation was ever published.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: What about 2015?
items.answer: The system didn't exist; the flood maps (NRSC, 4,001 polygons) that justify it are in our mirror.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: Is it working in NEM 2026 right now?
items.answer: Our probes run monthly; a forecast scorecard within 7 days of every activation is the standing protocol (ELI10 §10).

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: Why has no scorecard ever been published?
items.answer: No archive culture exists inside the system — F5. Scorecards need the forecast side; the system throws it away.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: Did warnings reach Velachery in Dec 2025?
items.answer: Unknowable from any public record. **RTI target:** activation logs + dissemination records.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: What about Red Hills (Puzhal) shutters?
items.answer: Opened for the sixth time that season in early Dec 2025; the system's sensors recorded the levels (REPORT §1, F8).

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: Did any forecast demonstrably save a life?
items.answer: Answer: **zero verified references** across 27 media entries (MEDIA-CLAIMS pattern 1). Not proof of failure — proof of no evidence.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: Was Ennore's 56 cm in 3 days forecast?
items.answer: No archive to check against. This question is exactly why F5 matters.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: How fresh is the water-level data during storms?
items.answer: AWLR runs near-live (to Aug 2026 in our pull); ARG open feed is stale to 2022 (F3) — the picture is per-sensor-type.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: Who got the credit in the press during Ditwah?
items.answer: IMD/RMC, CWC, district collectors, GCC's separate ICCC/EWS — not RTFF (MEDIA-CLAIMS entries 17–18).

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: What did the control room actually do during Ditwah?
items.answer: No public log. **RTI target:** HMCR activation log, Dec 2025.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: Could I have compared forecast vs rainfall myself last December?
items.answer: No — no forecast archive. From NEM 2026 onward, our scorecards will make that possible.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: Has the system ever been wrong in public?
items.answer: No public record of any forecast — so also no record of any miss. Silence isn't accuracy.

items.section: I. How it did in real storms
items.q: What's the first storm where a public scorecard is possible?
items.answer: NEM 2026 — if activations occur, we publish within 7 days. ---

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: Who staffs the control room?
items.answer: CRA/TNDRRA officers + SECON-JBA (handholding); actual staffing rosters are not public.

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: What is this "handholding phase"?
items.answer: WB-funded supervisory consultancy for the RTFF project ($0.10M line in TNCRUDP plans) — aftercare bought from the Bank, years after "operational".

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: Is the system dependent on consultants forever?
items.answer: The structure suggests yes (consultant-run activations + AMCs + handholding); no public exit/capacity-transfer plan exists.

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: What's an AMC?
items.answer: Annual Maintenance Contract — the vendor keeps sensors/software alive; expiry dates live in the registries we mirrored.

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: How many stations have an active AMC?
items.answer: 66 flagged `isamc=true`; expiry populated for only ~6 — calendar unknown (F10).

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: What does maintenance cost per year?
items.answer: RTI target: AMC payment records (TNUIFSL/WRD).

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: Who pays when the PDGF grant ends?
items.answer: Unresolved — likely TNCRUDP, but no public commitment. The "operating money unresolved at both ends" point (REPORT §5.5).

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: Is there a backup data centre?
items.answer: A Nearline Disaster Recovery Centre at WRD Chepauk is described on the portal.

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: Is there a public operations manual?
items.answer: No SOP published — recommendation-grade gap.

items.section: J. Maintenance and operations
items.q: What happens during a power/network failure in a cyclone?
items.answer: No public redundancy/continuity spec. ---

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: If it fails, who is answerable?
items.answer: CRA overall supervision per official structure; no published SLA, no named accountable officer.

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: What is TNDRRA?
items.answer: TN Disaster Risk Reduction Agency under the Commissionerate of Revenue Administration — the HMCR's home.

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: Does the elected council or MLAs oversee it?
items.answer: No visible elected oversight anywhere in the public record.

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: What is the Advisory Committee?
items.answer: Expert committee (IIT-M, IIT-B, NRSC, Anna University, NDMA-linked) formed 21 Jun 2021; its minutes are not public.

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: Is there a citizens' representative on it?
items.answer: None in any published membership list we've seen.

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: Has CAG looked at it?
items.answer: No public audit of this line exists. **Ask** for a performance audit.

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: Is it under RTI?
items.answer: Yes — CRA, WRD, TNUIFSL and GCC are public authorities; our §5.6 lists the targets.

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: Whose budget line does it sit under?
items.answer: WRD/PDGF/TNUIFSL mix; the exact ledger split is not public.

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: What happens when the government changes?
items.answer: Unknown — but the 2026 IFMC announcement suggests institutional memory survives via re-announcements, not via records.

items.section: K. Governance and oversight
items.q: Is there any legislative committee on urban flooding?
items.answer: Not in our sweep. (One for Assembly-watch.) ---

items.section: L. The old website and institutional memory
items.q: Was there an earlier website?
items.answer: `chennaifloodsdss.in` — same system, first web face, live by the 2021 pilot, footer "Developed and Maintained by SECON & JBA".

items.section: L. The old website and institutional memory
items.q: Why did it die?
items.answer: Quiet migration to the gov domain in 2025; domain now NXDOMAIN; no redirect, no notice, no archive notice (F9).

items.section: L. The old website and institutional memory
items.q: Where did its data go?
items.answer: Officially: nowhere. Practically: into our Dec-2023 mirror — 34,050 gauge readings incl. the full Michaung event.

items.section: L. The old website and institutional memory
items.q: Can I still see the old site?
items.answer: Partially via Wayback Machine (last capture 2025-08-31) and fully in our mirrors.

items.section: L. The old website and institutional memory
items.q: Is the new site better?
items.answer: Same data pattern, new domain; the bulletin set grew from 0 to 7 — otherwise the gaps carry over.

items.section: L. The old website and institutional memory
items.q: What else could vanish like this?
items.answer: Everything on it — which is why the project re-mirrors annually by design (ELI10 §4).

items.section: L. The old website and institutional memory
items.q: Could this happen to the new site too?
items.answer: Yes. F9 is a pattern, not an event. ---

items.section: M. The 2026 IFMC (Integrated Flood Management Centre)
items.q: What is the IFMC?
items.answer: A new centre announced Oct 2026 (Revenue & DM secretary, at NIOT forum) promising street-level flood prediction three days ahead — focused on Chennai first.

items.section: M. The 2026 IFMC (Integrated Flood Management Centre)
items.q: Is it new money?
items.answer: No cost stated in coverage. **Watch:** IFMC sanction/trail.

items.section: M. The 2026 IFMC (Integrated Flood Management Centre)
items.q: Is IFMC the same as RTFF & SDSS?
items.answer: The promise is verbatim RTFF's 2025 promise; the relationship (successor/expansion/rebrand) is publicly undefined.

items.section: M. The 2026 IFMC (Integrated Flood Management Centre)
items.q: Was the earlier promise ever finished before the new one launched?
items.answer: That is precisely the accountability question — one year after "fully operational", the same capability is being re-promised (MEDIA-CLAIMS pattern 3).

items.section: M. The 2026 IFMC (Integrated Flood Management Centre)
items.q: Should residents welcome or resist IFMC?
items.answer: Neither — demand the paper trail: what it adds, what it costs, and whether RTFF's gaps (F2–F7) are being fixed, not re-branded.

items.section: M. The 2026 IFMC (Integrated Flood Management Centre)
items.q: Will you track it?
items.answer: Yes — standing IFMC watch (ELI10 §10). ---

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: Do richer areas get better warnings?
items.answer: The seven named street-forecast zones span income levels; no equity analysis of alert delivery exists anywhere.

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: What about Ennore / north Chennai?
items.answer: Ennore's Dec 2025 disaster was *recorded* well by the system's own layers (56 cm/3 days, level-6 report) — but warning *delivery* there is undocumented.

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: Peripheral flood hotspots like Mudichur?
items.answer: Named in the street-forecast list; actual alert reach unknown.

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: Do resettlement-colony residents get alerts?
items.answer: No evidence of targeted design.

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: Is warning info available in Tamil?
items.answer: Partial — app claims multilingual; the substantive bulletins are English PDFs.

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: Do tenants get warned the same as owners?
items.answer: No differentiated mechanism exists.

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: Are informal settlements inside the model?
items.answer: Wards are; informal layouts are likely under-represented in cadastral layers — a research question we can test with the GIS mirror.

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: Do I need a smartphone to be warned?
items.answer: Effectively yes for TN-Alert — that's the digital-divide problem (alert equity, Q96–Q97).

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: Is there a phone hotline for flood help?
items.answer: GCC's 1913 complaint line (flood); a *forecasting* hotline does not exist.

items.section: N. Equity: who actually gets warned
items.q: Has anyone studied who received Dec-2025 warnings?
items.answer: Nobody — no delivery data is public. **RTI target.** ---

items.section: O. Comparisons and benchmarks
items.q: How does this compare with Mumbai's CFLOWS?
items.answer: CFLOWS (IIT-B for MCGM) is the usual benchmark; a cost-and-capability comparison is queued in our audit plan (B4) — no rigorous public comparison exists yet.

items.section: O. Comparisons and benchmarks
items.q: Kolkata?
items.answer: Kolkata's early-warning system (KEWS) exists with published alerts; comparative audit pending.

items.section: O. Comparisons and benchmarks
items.q: Bengaluru?
items.answer: Fragmented civic alerting; no comparable integrated DSS — part of why "first in India" claims go unchallenged.

items.section: O. Comparisons and benchmarks
items.q: What does global good practice look like?
items.answer: Japan/UK/Netherlands: published forecast archives, open APIs, post-event verification reports as routine.

items.section: O. Comparisons and benchmarks
items.q: Is ₹107 crore good value?
items.answer: Unanswerable until verification exists — that's the honest budget position, not a slogan.

items.section: O. Comparisons and benchmarks
items.q: What else could ₹107 crore have bought?
items.answer: Counterfactual framing queued (AUDIT-PLAN B4): desilted kilometres at unit rates, pump stations, gauge networks. The "fare-hike test" applied to data infrastructure.

items.section: O. Comparisons and benchmarks
items.q: How many flood-forecast stations does all of India have?
items.answer: CWC runs ~360 flood-forecast stations nationally (2026 preparedness conference figure) — Chennai's urban system is a different beast; comparisons need care. ---

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: Can I check whether my street will flood?
items.answer: Only via image-PDF maps during an activation, or the static 2021 ward-depth layer. No live street query exists for the public.

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: Where's my ward's data?
items.answer: All 200 wards are in our GIS mirror (`gcc_200_wards`, ward depth min/max — noting the 2021 stamp).

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: How do I read a bulletin?
items.answer: They're image PDFs; an explainer is on our list for the public page.

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: My area flooded but no alert came. What do I do?
items.answer: Document (photos+timestamp), complain on GCC 1913, and send us the record — evidence is how the scorecard gets built.

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: Can I report flooding to the system?
items.answer: The system has a crowdsourced-report layer (we mirrored 173 reports, identities stripped); GCC 1913 and IIT-M's citizen portal also collect reports.

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: Do citizen reports actually reach the model?
items.answer: The crowd layer feeds the dashboard; whether it enters forecasts isn't documented.

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: How deep was the water on my street in 2015?
items.answer: NRSC's 2015 extent (4,001 polygons) gives area-level depth bands — street-level granularity doesn't exist publicly.

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: Are my lake's levels public?
items.answer: Poondi, Chembarambakkam, Red Hills, Cholavaram storage are on the dashboard and in our mirror.

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: Can I build my own flood app on this data?
items.answer: Yes — that's what our HF datasets are for. (The government's own open feed is stale — F3 — so build on the mirror, and demand they fix theirs.)

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: Who do I complain to about a dead gauge?
items.answer: Start with GCC ward works + an RTI to CRA/WRD citing the station ID from our registries; the formal ask is a public station-status layer.

items.section: P. "What about MY street?" — practical questions
items.q: What should I actually do this monsoon?
items.answer: Follow IMD/RMC and collector advisories as primary; treat RTFF bulletins as one input; keep evidence (photos, dates); check our site for the scorecard after each activation. ---

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: What RTI should I file first?
items.answer: One line: *"Certified copy of the sanction order(s) for RTFF & SDSS Chennai under PDGF, with cost and revisions."* To PIO, WRD / CRA / Finance Dept. (REPORT §5.6 list.)

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: Which authority's PIO handles this?
items.answer: Three: WRD (basin/works), CRA/TNDRRA (control room), TNUIFSL (fund management) — and GCC for ward-level SWD.

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: What if the RTI is refused?
items.answer: First appeal to the departmental FAO, second appeal to the TN Information Commission. Refusals on "third-party information" are contestable for sanction orders.

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: Can the CAG audit it?
items.answer: Yes — citizens can request inclusion of RTFF & SDSS in a TN performance audit; cite F10's gaps.

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: Is there a World Bank grievance route?
items.answer: The Inspection Panel (and GRS) accept complaints from affected people on WB-financed operations; TNCRUDP is the current operation to cite.

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: Can I see procurement documents?
items.answer: WB-side plans are public (P179189); TNUIFSL tender files need RTI; award values have never been published.

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: Have MLAs/MPs asked questions about it?
items.answer: We haven't swept TN Assembly Q&A yet — queued watch.

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: Has any journalist investigated it?
items.answer: Launch coverage is universal; accountability coverage is effectively our project — MEDIA-CLAIMS documents the gap.

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: How do I use your evidence in a petition or story?
items.answer: REPORT (evidence-graded claims + ledger), MEDIA-CLAIMS (hype vs record), DATA-CATALOGUE (provenance) are built to be citable, with sources.

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: Can resident welfare associations file jointly?
items.answer: Any citizen may file; RWAs can bundle RTIs (sanction order + AMC payments + activation logs are three clean, unjoinable asks).

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: What's the single highest-leverage ask?
items.answer: **Publish the forecast archive.** Every other question becomes answerable once forecasts are kept and comparable to observations (F5).

items.section: Q. The accountability toolkit
items.q: How do I track whether things improve?
items.answer: Project hub + the quarterly RTFF-DSS Ledger; monthly probes; per-activation scorecards (ELI10 §10). ---

items.section: R. Privacy and surveillance
items.q: Does the system track me personally?
items.answer: The sensor telemetry is environmental, not personal; the crowdsourced layer did carry usernames — we stripped them before publishing.

items.section: R. Privacy and surveillance
items.q: Are CCTV feeds part of it?
items.answer: GCC's ICCC (separate system) integrates CCTV; RTFF's AboutUs describes CCTV-equipped control rooms — camera governance is a different audit.

items.section: R. Privacy and surveillance
items.q: Does TN-Alert collect my location?
items.answer: Unknown — the app has no published privacy policy we could find. A fair question to put to TNSDMA.

items.section: R. Privacy and surveillance
items.q: Are citizen flood reports public?
items.answer: Yes — 173 reports (Nov–Dec 2025) are in our mirror, scrubbed of identities.

items.section: R. Privacy and surveillance
items.q: Should I worry about my name in flood reports?
items.answer: In our release, no (scrubbed). In the government's original system, retention policy is unpublished — ask. ---

items.section: S. The basin: drains, lakes, wetlands
items.q: Why not just fix drains instead of buying forecasts?
items.answer: Both/and. GCC's FY2026-27 climate budget is ₹1,341 crore for 240+ km of SWD; forecasting without working drains is a thermometer for a broken pipe. The desk supports both, verified.

items.section: S. The basin: drains, lakes, wetlands
items.q: Are encroachments the real problem?
items.answer: Partially — hydrology vs ecology debates (Pallikaranai, wetland loss) are real; a forecasting model cannot de-encroach. It can, however, expose where build-overs worsen inundation — if its data were open.

items.section: S. The basin: drains, lakes, wetlands
items.q: Does the model include the storm-drain network?
items.answer: SWD layers are model inputs (in our GIS mirror); drain *maintenance* status is not modelled — it's a GCC works question.

items.section: S. The basin: drains, lakes, wetlands
items.q: Who desilts, and when?
items.answer: GCC pre-monsoon works, claimed 95% complete before NEM 2026 (press, graded C); independent verification is absent.

items.section: S. The basin: drains, lakes, wetlands
items.q: What about Pallikaranai and the wetlands?
items.answer: The marsh is a mapped layer in our mirror; NGT-driven protection orders are recent news — the flood model and the ecology fight are two fronts of the same basin story.

items.section: S. The basin: drains, lakes, wetlands
items.q: The Kosasthalaiyar floods north Chennai differently than the Adyar floods the south. Does the forecast know that?
items.answer: The model covers both basins separately, but their public outputs arrive in the same PDF — basin-level separation that a Manali resident and a Velachery resident both need is achievable from existing layers if they were published as data.

items.section: S. The basin: drains, lakes, wetlands
items.q: After everything we've read: what is the single question I should ask my MLA?
items.answer: "Where is the archive of this system's forecasts, and when will it be public?" — every other number in this document flows from that one answer. உங்கள் சொத்து.
